newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-SESTRIERE ORGANISERS IN CONFIDENT MOOD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SESTRIERE ORGANISERS IN CONFIDENT MOOD.

text.p: Organisers of the 1997 Sestriere Alpine skiing world championships said on Tuesday that preparations for the event were on schedule.
Giovanni Agnelli Jr., president of the organising committee, told a news conference that work for the February 2-15 championships was proceeding well.
"Despite a few delays at the start, work is going ahead according to plan and everything should be ready by the start to welcome the athletes, organisers and media," he said.
Recent world championships have been seriously disrupted, with the last ones in Sierra Nevada, Spain, being postponed for a year to 1996 due to a lack of snow in 1995.
The previous 1993 championships in Morioka, Japan, were repeatedly disrupted by high winds and bad weather.
Sestriere organisers said some 400 billion lire ($280 million) had been spent on the championships, mostly connected with road building projects and hotel construction.
Officials said that state funding had covered $63 million of the costs with the rest provided by local government, the European Union and private enterprise sponsors.
The Sestriere world championships will have nightime floodlit slaloms for both men and women while a completely new giant slalom piste has also been built.
